elements.name: BatteryManagementSystem
elements.label: Battery management
elements.blurb: Watches every cell: charge level, temperature, and protection limits.

elements.name: BrakeSystem
elements.label: Brakes
elements.blurb: Discs and calipers at each wheel, blended with motor regeneration.

elements.name: ChargingSystem
elements.label: Charging port
elements.blurb: Charge door and socket. Manages the handshake with a charging station.

elements.name: ServiceDiagnosticsSystem
elements.label: Diagnostics port
elements.blurb: The service connector a technician plugs into to read faults and telemetry.

elements.name: EnergyStorageSystem
elements.label: Battery pack
elements.blurb: The skateboard battery under the floor. Stores the energy for range and acceleration.

elements.name: DriverInterfaceSystem
elements.label: Driver interface
elements.blurb: Dashboard, steering wheel, pedals and screen. How the driver commands and observes the car.

elements.name: TractionInverter
elements.label: Traction inverter
elements.blurb: Converts battery DC into the AC the motor needs, and sets how hard the motor pushes.

elements.name: PowertrainSystem
elements.label: Powertrain
elements.blurb: Electric motors, reduction gears and half-shafts that turn electricity into motion.

elements.name: Usable Battery Energy
elements.text: The EnergyStorageSystem shall provide at least 82 kWh of usable battery energy at beginning of life.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Usable battery energy is >= 82 kWh.

elements.name: State-of-Charge Estimation
elements.text: The BatteryManagementSystem shall estimate state of charge with an error of no more than plus or minus 3 percentage points over the defined operating range.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: SOC estimate error is within +/-3 percentage points.

elements.name: Battery Protection
elements.text: The BatteryManagementSystem shall inhibit operation outside defined cell voltage and temperature safety limits.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Out-of-limit stimulus causes protective inhibit/isolation behavior.

elements.name: Traction Power Capability
elements.text: The EnergyStorageSystem shall supply at least 135 kW of traction electrical power for 10 seconds at the nominal performance test state of charge.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Delivered traction power is >= 135 kW for >= 10 s.

elements.name: Regenerative Charge Acceptance
elements.text: The EnergyStorageSystem shall accept regenerative charging power when state-of-charge, voltage, and temperature limits permit.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Regenerative power is accepted under permitted conditions and limited outside them.

elements.name: Brake Command Response
elements.text: The BrakeSystem shall begin producing commanded braking action within 100 ms of receiving a valid BrakeCommand.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Braking response begins <= 100 ms.

elements.name: Blended Braking
elements.text: The BrakeSystem shall support blended regenerative and friction braking commands provided by vehicle control.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Blended braking maintains requested deceleration while using available regeneration.

elements.name: Fail-Safe Friction Braking
elements.text: The BrakeSystem shall retain friction-braking capability when regenerative braking is unavailable.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Friction braking remains available with regenerative path disabled.

elements.name: DC Fast-Charge Coordination
elements.text: The ChargingSystem shall coordinate a compatible DC fast-charge session and request charging power only when battery and vehicle-state prerequisites permit.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Charge session starts only when prerequisites are valid and is inhibited otherwise.

elements.name: Drive Request Validation
elements.text: The VehicleControlSystem shall validate driver acceleration requests against vehicle state and active limits before issuing a torque command.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Invalid/out-of-range requests are rejected or limited before torque command publication.

elements.name: Control Command Latency
elements.text: The VehicleControlSystem shall publish a validated torque command within 50 ms of receiving the required driver and vehicle-state inputs.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Validated torque command publication latency is <= 50 ms.

elements.name: Fault Detection and Derating
elements.text: The VehicleControlSystem shall detect configured critical faults and command defined derating or fault-state behavior.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Configured fault produces the required derating/fault command.

elements.name: Brake Coordination
elements.text: The VehicleControlSystem shall coordinate regenerative and friction braking requests while preserving the requested total deceleration within system limits.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Combined braking tracks requested deceleration within defined tolerance.

elements.name: Driver Status Presentation
elements.text: The DriverInterfaceSystem shall display Ready state, vehicle speed, battery state of charge, active drive mode, and safety-relevant faults.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: All required status items are visible and correspond to model/runtime state.

elements.name: Start Command Capture
elements.text: The DriverInterfaceSystem shall capture a valid driver start request and provide it to VehicleControlSystem through the typed driver-command interface.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Valid start request produces a typed StartCommand input to vehicle control.

elements.name: High-Voltage Power Interface
elements.text: The EnergyStorageSystem-to-PowertrainSystem high-voltage interface shall provide compatible voltage, current, isolation, and connector typing for traction power transfer.
elements.rationale: Controls an explicit subsystem boundary and enables integration/change-impact analysis.
elements.acceptance: Both interface ends use HighVoltagePowerInterface and the conveyed power item is compatible.

elements.name: Torque Command Interface
elements.text: The VehicleControlSystem-to-PowertrainSystem torque-command interface shall convey a typed torque request without type mismatch.
elements.rationale: Controls an explicit subsystem boundary and enables integration/change-impact analysis.
elements.acceptance: Both endpoints use TorqueCommandInterface and the ItemFlow conveys TorqueCommandData.

elements.name: Sensor Data Interface
elements.text: The VehicleSensorSystem-to-VehicleControlSystem interface shall convey typed vehicle-state sensor data.
elements.rationale: Controls an explicit subsystem boundary and enables integration/change-impact analysis.
elements.acceptance: Both endpoints use SensorDataInterface and the ItemFlow conveys SensorData.

elements.name: Brake Command Interface
elements.text: The VehicleControlSystem-to-BrakeSystem interface shall convey a typed braking command.
elements.rationale: Controls an explicit subsystem boundary and enables integration/change-impact analysis.
elements.acceptance: Both endpoints use BrakeCommandInterface and the ItemFlow conveys BrakeCommandData.

elements.name: Thermal Interface
elements.text: The EnergyStorageSystem and PowertrainSystem shall exchange thermal energy/coolant through interfaces compatible with ThermalFluidInterface.
elements.rationale: Controls an explicit subsystem boundary and enables integration/change-impact analysis.
elements.acceptance: Thermal connector endpoints use compatible ThermalFluidInterface typing.

elements.name: Charging Power Interface
elements.text: The charging path shall use a typed ChargePowerInterface between vehicle boundary, ChargingSystem, and EnergyStorageSystem.
elements.rationale: Controls an explicit subsystem boundary and enables integration/change-impact analysis.
elements.acceptance: Charge path endpoints use compatible ChargePowerInterface typing.

elements.name: Diagnostic Service Interface
elements.text: The vehicle service boundary, ServiceDiagnosticsSystem, and VehicleControlSystem shall use a typed DiagnosticServiceInterface.
elements.rationale: Controls an explicit subsystem boundary and enables integration/change-impact analysis.
elements.acceptance: Diagnostic connector endpoints use compatible DiagnosticServiceInterface typing.

elements.name: Driver Command Interface
elements.text: The vehicle driver boundary, DriverInterfaceSystem, and VehicleControlSystem shall use a typed DriverCommandInterface.
elements.rationale: Controls an explicit subsystem boundary and enables integration/change-impact analysis.
elements.acceptance: Driver-command connector endpoints use compatible DriverCommandInterface typing.

elements.name: Tractive Force
elements.text: The propulsion system shall provide at least 4500 N of tractive force at the defined nominal launch analysis point.
elements.rationale: Provides a measurable engineering target traceable to architecture, analysis, and verification.
elements.acceptance: Calculated tractive force is >= 4500 N.

elements.name: Electrical Traction Power
elements.text: The propulsion system shall support at least 135 kW of electrical traction power at the defined nominal performance point.
elements.rationale: Provides a measurable engineering target traceable to architecture, analysis, and verification.
elements.acceptance: Calculated electrical traction power is >= 135 kW.

elements.name: Nominal Range Margin
elements.text: The vehicle energy architecture shall analytically demonstrate at least 400 km of nominal range using usable battery energy and nominal consumption.
elements.rationale: Provides a measurable engineering target traceable to architecture, analysis, and verification.
elements.acceptance: Range analysis result is >= 400 km.

elements.name: Regenerative Braking
elements.text: The propulsion and energy systems shall accept at least 50 kW of regenerative braking power when battery and traction limits permit.
elements.rationale: Provides a measurable engineering target traceable to architecture, analysis, and verification.
elements.acceptance: Accepted regenerative power is >= 50 kW under valid regen conditions.

elements.name: Top Speed
elements.text: The vehicle shall achieve at least 160 km/h under nominal mass, battery, tire, and environmental conditions.
elements.rationale: Provides a measurable engineering target traceable to architecture, analysis, and verification.
elements.acceptance: Measured top speed is >= 160 km/h.

elements.name: Gradeability
elements.text: The vehicle shall sustain 30 km/h on a 20 percent grade under nominal mass and battery conditions.
elements.rationale: Provides a measurable engineering target traceable to architecture, analysis, and verification.
elements.acceptance: Vehicle sustains >= 30 km/h on a 20% grade for the specified duration.

elements.name: Torque Conversion
elements.text: The PowertrainSystem shall convert supplied high-voltage electrical power into commanded traction torque at the motor output.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Measured motor/wheel torque follows valid command.

elements.name: Power Conversion Efficiency
elements.text: The traction inverter shall achieve at least 95 percent conversion efficiency at the nominal analysis point.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Inverter conversion efficiency is >= 95%.

elements.name: Torque Command Response
elements.text: The PowertrainSystem shall begin responding to a new valid torque command within 20 ms.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Torque response begins <= 20 ms after command receipt.

elements.name: Fault Torque Limiting
elements.text: The PowertrainSystem shall limit or remove propulsion torque after receipt of a confirmed critical propulsion fault.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Critical propulsion fault results in defined torque limit/removal.

elements.name: Vehicle Speed Accuracy
elements.text: The VehicleSensorSystem shall estimate vehicle speed with an error no greater than plus or minus 1 km/h over the defined operating range.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Speed estimate error is within +/-1 km/h.

elements.name: Sensor Plausibility Detection
elements.text: The VehicleSensorSystem shall identify configured implausible wheel-speed input conditions within 100 ms.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Configured implausible input is detected <= 100 ms.

elements.name: Service Data Access
elements.text: The ServiceDiagnosticsSystem shall provide authorized access to required DTCs and live telemetry through the typed diagnostic-service interface.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Authorized session reads required DTCs and telemetry; unauthorized session is rejected.

elements.name: Safe Controlled Transportation
elements.text: The electric vehicle shall provide controlled transportation and shall transition to a safe operating state when a critical vehicle fault is detected.
elements.rationale: Safety is the governing stakeholder objective for all vehicle behavior.
elements.acceptance: Critical-fault injection results in a defined safe/degraded state without uncontrolled propulsion.

elements.name: Nominal Driving Range
elements.text: The electric vehicle shall provide at least 400 km of nominal driving range on a fully usable battery under the defined nominal drive cycle.
elements.rationale: Range is a primary customer-value and sizing driver for the energy system.
elements.acceptance: Calculated or measured nominal range is >= 400 km.

elements.name: Responsive Acceleration
elements.text: The electric vehicle shall accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in 7.0 seconds or less at nominal mass, battery state, and environmental conditions.
elements.rationale: Acceleration sets the required tractive-force and power envelope.
elements.acceptance: 0-100 km/h elapsed time is <= 7.0 s under nominal test conditions.

elements.name: Convenient Charging
elements.text: The electric vehicle shall support compatible DC fast charging from 10 percent to 80 percent state of charge in 35 minutes or less under nominal battery temperature.
elements.rationale: Charging time materially affects vehicle availability and customer acceptance.
elements.acceptance: 10%-80% SOC charge time is <= 35 minutes at nominal battery temperature.

elements.name: Energy Efficiency
elements.text: The electric vehicle shall consume no more than 0.20 kWh per km over the defined nominal drive cycle.
elements.rationale: Energy efficiency drives range, battery sizing, and operating cost.
elements.acceptance: Nominal-cycle energy consumption is <= 0.20 kWh/km.

elements.name: Intuitive Driver Operation
elements.text: The electric vehicle shall allow the driver to start, drive, brake, stop, and observe vehicle status using a consistent set of driver controls and indications.
elements.rationale: The vehicle must expose complex system behavior through a simple operating interface.
elements.acceptance: Driver can complete start-drive-brake-stop workflow and observe required status indications without service intervention.

elements.name: Serviceability and Diagnostics
elements.text: The electric vehicle shall provide service personnel with diagnostic trouble codes, vehicle status, and subsystem telemetry through an authorized diagnostic interface.
elements.rationale: Fast fault isolation reduces maintenance time and lifecycle cost.
elements.acceptance: Authorized service session can read active/stored DTCs and required telemetry.

elements.name: Resilient Degraded Operation
elements.text: The electric vehicle shall preserve controllability through defined degraded operating modes when a recoverable subsystem fault occurs.
elements.rationale: Graceful degradation prevents a single recoverable fault from becoming a hazardous loss of function.
elements.acceptance: Injected recoverable faults result in defined derating/degraded behavior while controllability is preserved.

elements.name: Commanded Startup
elements.text: The vehicle shall enter the Ready state within 2.0 seconds after receiving a valid StartCommand when startup prerequisites are satisfied.
elements.rationale: Predictable startup behavior connects driver intent to executable control behavior.
elements.acceptance: Ready state is reached <= 2.0 s after a valid command.

elements.name: Propulsion Delivery
elements.text: The vehicle shall deliver commanded positive and negative wheel torque within validated operating limits.
elements.rationale: This is the central traction function required to meet vehicle performance.
elements.acceptance: Measured wheel torque tracks validated command within defined operating limits.

elements.name: Energy Storage
elements.text: The vehicle shall provide at least 82 kWh of usable traction-energy storage at beginning of life.
elements.rationale: Usable battery energy establishes the analytical basis for the range requirement.
elements.acceptance: Usable traction energy is >= 82 kWh.

elements.name: Controlled Braking
elements.text: The vehicle shall initiate commanded braking within 100 ms of a valid driver or vehicle-control braking request.
elements.rationale: Brake response time is a direct controllability and safety requirement.
elements.acceptance: Brake-system response begins <= 100 ms after valid command receipt.

elements.name: Thermal Control
elements.text: The vehicle shall actively control battery, inverter, motor, and charging thermal conditions within their defined operating envelopes.
elements.rationale: Thermal control protects performance, battery life, and electrical safety.
elements.acceptance: Monitored component temperatures remain within specified operating envelopes.

elements.name: Vehicle State Estimation
elements.text: The vehicle shall provide control functions with valid estimates of vehicle speed, battery state of charge, and critical temperatures.
elements.rationale: Closed-loop control and fault management depend on trusted vehicle state data.
elements.acceptance: Required state estimates are available, plausible, and within specified accuracy limits.

elements.name: Driver Information and Controls
elements.text: The vehicle shall present drive state, speed, state of charge, active drive mode, and safety-relevant faults to the driver.
elements.rationale: Driver awareness is required for normal operation and fault response.
elements.acceptance: All required status items are visible and update when model/runtime values change.

elements.name: Charge Management
elements.text: The vehicle shall coordinate compatible AC/DC charging and shall inhibit traction propulsion while the vehicle is in an active charging state.
elements.rationale: Charging must be coordinated with vehicle state and high-voltage safety.
elements.acceptance: Compatible charging session is controlled and traction torque remains inhibited while Charging is active.

elements.name: Diagnostic Management
elements.text: The vehicle shall detect, timestamp, store, and report diagnostic trouble codes for monitored subsystem faults.
elements.rationale: Structured diagnostics enable rapid maintenance and traceable fault history.
elements.acceptance: Injected monitored faults create readable timestamped DTC records.

elements.name: High-Voltage Isolation
elements.text: The vehicle shall open the high-voltage traction path when a confirmed isolation fault or crash isolation request is present.
elements.rationale: High-voltage isolation protects occupants and service personnel.
elements.acceptance: HV traction path is de-energized after confirmed isolation/crash request within the defined safety time.

elements.name: Fault Management
elements.text: The vehicle shall transition to a defined Fault or Degraded state within 500 ms after confirmation of a critical monitored fault.
elements.rationale: A bounded reaction time makes fault behavior deterministic and verifiable.
elements.acceptance: Confirmed critical fault causes Fault/Degraded transition <= 500 ms.

elements.name: Interface Integrity
elements.text: The vehicle shall use typed and compatible interfaces for power, commands, sensor data, thermal exchange, charging, diagnostics, and driver input.
elements.rationale: Typed interfaces are the basis for integration control and model-based impact analysis.
elements.acceptance: All modeled connector endpoints use compatible typed interfaces and all ItemFlows resolve to their connectors.

elements.name: Battery Temperature Control
elements.text: The ThermalManagementSystem shall maintain battery temperature between 15 and 40 degrees Celsius during nominal propulsion and charging operation.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Battery temperature remains 15-40 C during nominal thermal test.

elements.name: Power Electronics Cooling
elements.text: The ThermalManagementSystem shall maintain inverter and motor temperatures below their modeled operating limits during the nominal performance profile.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Inverter and motor temperatures remain below modeled limits.

elements.name: Thermal Pump Control
elements.text: The ThermalController shall command coolant-pump operation as a function of modeled thermal load and component temperature.
elements.rationale: Allocates a system-level requirement to an implementable subsystem or component.
elements.acceptance: Pump command changes consistently with thermal-load/temperature conditions.
